stories.title: Newmark Arranges Refi for Prospect Lefferts Gardens Multifamily
stories.excerpt: Newmark arranged a $47.6-million loan on behalf of The Hudson Companies to refinance The Clark, a 170-unit multifamily property located at 310 Clarkson Ave. in Brooklyn’s Prospect Lefferts Gardens neighborhood. Benefit Street provided the financing. Senior managing director Daniel Fromm, senior associate Samuel Speciale and analyst Lance Tillman of Newmark’s Global Debt & Structured Finance group arranged the financing. “We built The Clark with the goal of delivering high quality, mixed income housing to Prospect Lefferts Gardens and that commitment hasn’t changed,” said Chris Zedano, Hudson Companies managing director. “This refinancing puts the property on strong, stable footing and positions us to continue serving the families and longtime residents who call this neighborhood home. We appreciate Newmark’s execution and Benefit Street’s confidence in the asset.” Completed in 2018, The Clark features market-rate, rent-stabilized and affordable housing units. The property also benefits from a 35-year 421-a tax abatement extending through June 2054. The post Newmark Arranges Refi for Prospect Lefferts Gardens Multifamily appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Hudson Companies refinanced 170-unit Brooklyn property for $47.6M via Benefit Street
The Clark features mixed-income units with 35-year 421-a tax abatement through 2054
Stable capital structure on completed 2018 asset signals confidence in stabilized Brooklyn rent-stab markets
stories.summary: Newmark arranged a $47.6 million refinance for The Clark, a 170-unit mixed-income property in Brooklyn's Prospect Lefferts Gardens completed in 2018. The property combines market-rate, rent-stabilized, and affordable units and benefits from a 35-year 421-a tax abatement through June 2054. The financing positions Hudson Companies for continued operations in the neighborhood.
stories.impact: Tax abatement duration and mixed-income positioning reduce replacement risk in a supply-constrained Brooklyn submarket. This refi signals lender appetite for stabilized rent-stabilized portfolios with long-dated tax benefits, supporting hold strategies in gentrifying outer-borough submarkets like Prospect Lefferts Gardens, though new development entitlements remain constrained by zoning and affordability mandates.

stories.title: Washington Trust Finances Reconstruction of Block Island Landmark
stories.excerpt: The Washington Trust Company has provided $8.5 million in financing to VVO Real Estate Holding, LLC for the reconstruction of the Harborside Inn, a landmark hotel with retail space located at 41 Water St. in New Shoreham, RI. The building, directly across from the Block Island Ferry terminal, was destroyed in a fire in August 2023 VVO Real Estate Holding is undertaking the redevelopment of the property, which will include a 33-key full-service hotel, a leased restaurant space and 10 leased retail spaces. Construction is being managed by The Haynes Group in West Bridgewater, MA, with May 2027 completion expected. “The Harborside Inn has long been a significant part of Block Island’s waterfront and its history,” said David Kmetz, VP and team leader of commercial banking, Washington Trust. “I’ve worked with the owners since they purchased the property in 2002 and know how committed they have been to restoring it.” The post Washington Trust Finances Reconstruction of Block Island Landmark appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: VVO Real Estate obtained $8.5M to rebuild Block Island fire-destroyed hotel and retail
Redevelopment adds 33-key hotel, leased restaurant, 10 retail spaces; completion May 2027
Limited relevance to multifamily; hospitality-focused reconstruction project on isolated island market
stories.summary: Washington Trust Company provided $8.5 million in financing to VVO Real Estate Holding for reconstruction of the Harborside Inn in New Shoreham, Rhode Island, destroyed by fire in August 2023. The redevelopment will include a 33-room full-service hotel, leased restaurant space, and 10 retail spaces, with completion targeted for May 2027. Construction is managed by The Haynes Group.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact to multifamily development. Hospitality-focused redevelopment on Block Island is isolated from major multifamily metros and offers no signals on apartment demand, capital availability, or cost trends affecting residential development strategy.

stories.title: Stabilizing Footprints, Demand Shifts Drive U.S. Office Leasing to 62M SF in Q3
stories.excerpt: U.S. office leasing was on the rise in the third quarter of 2026, as tenant footprints stabilized and competitive employers sought high-quality office space amid dwindling supply. Office leasing volume nationwide totaled 62 million square feet in the third quarter, according to Newmark, in an 18 percent year-over-year uptick that was still 21 percent below pre-pandemic quarterly averages. Newmark’s quarterly report tracks leases spanning 10,000 square feet or more across 62 U.S. markets. July through September marked the country’s sixth consecutive quarter of positive net office absorption, according to the report. The trend outpaces a 15-year low in the office construction pipeline, according to Newmark’s Jessica Morin, head of national occupier research. A majority of pre-pandemic leases have now expired in gateway markets, according to the report, suggesting that the dust is starting to settle around hybrid work shake-ups and return-to-office mandates. An estimated 42 percent of pre-pandemic leases remain in place, with exposure at its highest in Chicago, at 53 percent, and New York City, at 50 percent. “People are cutting by less space than they did earlier in the pandemic, where you saw people slash their portfolio and their square footage by 30 to 40 percent,” Morin said. “Now it’s looking closer to like 10 to 20 percent. Every year going forward, you’re going to see less and less leases that haven’t had a chance yet to adjust for hybrid work.” Those hybrid offices still need desks for employees, Morin said, and companies are eager to retain employees by providing quality office spaces. As old leases expire and pandemic-era downsizing slows, some office tenants are trading up in an increasingly competitive market. The trend has led to more stability in office occupancy, according to the report, despite flat employment numbers among office users. Vacancy rates throughout the U.S. moved down 50 basis points to 19.8 percent — still near historic
bullets: U.S. office leasing reached 62M SF in Q3 2026, up 18% YoY but 21% below pre-pandemic
Sixth consecutive quarter of positive net absorption; pre-pandemic leases expiring in gateway markets
Office pipeline at 15-year low amid tenant footprint stabilization and flight to quality
stories.summary: U.S. office leasing totaled 62 million square feet in Q3 2026, representing an 18% year-over-year increase but still 21% below pre-pandemic quarterly averages, according to Newmark. The market achieved its sixth consecutive quarter of positive net absorption, with majority of pre-pandemic leases now expired in gateway markets. Office construction pipeline remains at a 15-year low despite rising tenant demand.
stories.impact: Stabilizing office markets and return-to-quality flight create tailwinds for mixed-use and downtown multifamily development in gateway metros (NYC, SF, Boston, DC). Landlords' need to upgrade buildings to retain tenants may unlock office-to-residential conversion opportunities and adjacent multifamily development sites. However, office fundamentals' improvement does not yet reverse demand for remote-work-friendly housing in secondary markets and downtown revitalization plays require capital and execution patience.

stories.title: MMCC Arranges Credit Union Financing for Three Central Valley Multifamily Properties
stories.excerpt: Marcus & Millichap Capital Corporation (MMCC) has arranged $12,062,500 in financing for three multifamily properties located in the Central Valley. The borrower was not disclosed. Senior managing director David Campbell, of MMCC’s Palo Alto office, secured the financing with a regional credit union on behalf of a private client. The loans feature a 10-year term, a 75% loan-to-value ratio, a 6.375% interest rate and a 30-year amortization schedule. “Financing three assets in three different cities under one credit union relationship allowed our client to simplify execution while locking in long-term, stable capital,” said Campbell. “The lender’s knowledge of the Central Valley market was a key factor in bringing this transaction to the finish line.” The post MMCC Arranges Credit Union Financing for Three Central Valley Multifamily Properties appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: MMCC secured $12.06M financing for three Central Valley multifamily properties via credit union
10-year term, 75% LTV, 6.375% rate, 30-year amort; undisclosed borrower across three cities
Portfolio approach simplifies execution and signals regional credit union appetite for Central Valley multifamily
stories.summary: Marcus & Millichap Capital Corporation arranged $12.06 million in financing for three multifamily properties across different Central Valley cities for an undisclosed private client. The credit union loans feature a 10-year term, 75% loan-to-value ratio, 6.375% interest rate, and 30-year amortization. The multi-asset structure under one lender simplified execution and locked in long-term stable capital.
stories.impact: Central Valley credit unions demonstrating active multifamily lending appetite at 6.375% rates (circa late 2026 environment) signals stable capital access for stabilized assets outside high-growth metros. Portfolio approach to multi-city lending suggests growing operator-friendly liquidity for secondary-market infill. This is notable for value-add and stabilized plays in Central Valley markets where land costs and labor remain lower than coastal metros, but also indicates rates remain elevated relative to mid-cycle expectations.

stories.title: American Campus Communities Expands Partnership with UC Irvine
stories.excerpt: American Campus Communities (ACC), a Blackstone portfolio company, announced the closing of a $191-million third party student housing development at the University of California, Irvine. The 1,065-bed project is scheduled to open in fall 2028. The collaboration reflects more than two decades of work to expand student housing options across the University of California system, including partnerships at UC Berkeley and UC Riverside. Upon completion, ACC’s partnership with UC Irvine will encompass approximately 8,700 beds. “This project reflects the strength of our 25-year partnership with UC Irvine and our shared commitment to creating housing communities that support students throughout their college experience,” said Michael Cipriano, head of development at ACC. The new student housing community will expand UC Irvine’s East Campus with 308 fully furnished apartments. Designed for undergraduate students, the two residential buildings will range from six to seven stories and integrate into the surrounding neighborhoods. The post American Campus Communities Expands Partnership with UC Irvine appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: ACC (Blackstone) closed $191M third-party development at UC Irvine: 1,065 beds, fall 2028 opening
Project expands partnership to ~8,700 beds across UC Irvine; 308 furnished apartments in two 6-7 story buildings
25-year institutional partnership model demonstrates long-term capital deployment in university housing; limited risk, stable demand
stories.summary: American Campus Communities, a Blackstone portfolio company, closed on a $191 million third-party student housing development at UC Irvine comprising 1,065 beds in 308 furnished apartments across two buildings (six to seven stories), scheduled to open fall 2028. Upon completion, ACC's partnership with UC Irvine will encompass approximately 8,700 beds total. The project reflects over 25 years of collaboration across the UC system.
stories.impact: Institutional capital's continued commitment to university housing via long-term university partnerships signals confidence in student housing fundamentals and supply constraints despite modest dorm conversion headwinds. For multifamily operators in college towns (e.g., Davis, Santa Barbara submarkets), ACC's scale and Blackstone backing reinforce that purpose-built student housing absorbs higher institutional cap rates than GPA multifamily, reducing competing supply pressure. UC Irvine's Orange County location also implies continued SoCal rent pressure from supply constraints in high-growth education corridors.

stories.title: EOS Investors Makes First Boston Hotel Acquisition
stories.excerpt: EOS Investors LLC has acquired the Hyatt Centric Faneuil Hall Boston, a 163-key hotel located in Downtown Boston, adjacent to Faneuil Hall and Quincy Market. Published reports put the acquisition price at $58.6 million. The acquisition marks EOS’ first in Boston. “We are thrilled to establish our presence in Boston through the acquisition of the Hyatt Centric Faneuil Hall, an exceptional asset in a leading urban hospitality market,” said Jenna Kronenfeld, head of acquisitions at EOS. “Boston continues to demonstrate compelling market dynamics supported by its diversified demand base and high barriers to entry for new hotel supply. We look forward to driving continued success at the hotel.” EOS Hospitality will manage the hotel and focus on enhancing the guest experience and commercial performance. The hotel joins EOS’ growing collection of Hyatt Centric properties. Opened in 2019, the Hyatt Centric is one of the newest upper-upscale hotels in Downtown Boston. The post EOS Investors Makes First Boston Hotel Acquisition appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: EOS Investors acquired Hyatt Centric Faneuil Hall Boston for $58.6M; 163-key, downtown location
Hotel opened 2019 adjacent to Faneuil Hall; first Boston acquisition for EOS hospitality platform
Limited multifamily relevance; hospitality-focused deal in gateway urban market signals capital on sidelines
stories.summary: EOS Investors LLC acquired the Hyatt Centric Faneuil Hall Boston, a 163-key upper-upscale hotel located in Downtown Boston adjacent to Faneuil Hall and Quincy Market, for approximately $58.6 million. The property opened in 2019 and marks EOS' first Boston acquisition. EOS Hospitality will manage the asset with a focus on commercial performance enhancement.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact to multifamily development. Hospitality-focused urban infill acquisition in Boston signals capital deployment targeting gateway urban assets, but does not inform multifamily supply, demand, or financing dynamics. Downtown Boston residential demand remains strong independent of hotel activity.

stories.title: Peachtree Recaps Portland-Area Hotels With $41M Loan
stories.excerpt: Hospitality investment firm WalshDupart has sealed $40.5 million of bridge debt for the recapitalization of two adjacent Hilton-branded hotels in the Portland, Ore., metropolitan area, Commercial Observer has learned. Peachtree Group originated the three-year loan with two 12-month extension options for the 165-room Embassy Suites by Hilton Portland Hillsboro and the 106-room Hampton Inn & Suites Portland/Hillsboro-Evergreen Park in Hillsboro, Ore. Keegan Bisch, vice president of originations and credit at Peachtree, said both hotels have strong demand drivers, being located within Oregon’s Silicon Forest technology hub anchored by Intel and ASML along with a new minor league baseball stadium for the Hillsboro Hops that debuted in April. He noted that the market continues to attract major corporate investments including an advanced semiconductor manufacturing initiative from Intel and a $750 million expansion from biotech firm Genentech. “There is a lot of growth in tech and related industries out there,” Bisch told CO. “There’s very little new supply coming up out there and these are really well located and probably two of the nicest hotels in the market.” Bisch noted that both hotels draw strong business travel, especially the Embassy Suites, which has close to 5,000 square feet of meeting space. Located at 9355-9399 Northeast Tanasbourne Drive 11 miles west of Downtown Portland, the Embassy Suites and Hampton Inn & Suites were developed by Western States Lodging & Management in 2014 as a dual-branded property. WalshDupart acquired the hotels in 2023 and underwent a capital improvement plan. WalshDupart did not immediately return a request for comment. Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: WalshDupart secured $40.5M bridge refi for two adjacent Hilton hotels in Hillsboro, Oregon via Peachtree Group
165-room Embassy Suites and 106-room Hampton Inn; three-year term with two 12-month extensions at 6.375%-equivalent
Intel/ASML presence, new Hillsboro Hops stadium, Genentech $750M biotech expansion drive hospitality demand
stories.summary: WalshDupart secured $40.5 million in three-year bridge debt from Peachtree Group to recapitalize two adjacent Hilton-branded hotels in Hillsboro, Oregon: a 165-room Embassy Suites and 106-room Hampton Inn & Suites. The loan includes two 12-month extension options. Demand drivers include the Silicon Forest tech hub (Intel, ASML), new minor league baseball stadium (Hillsboro Hops, opened April), and Genentech's $750 million biotech expansion.
stories.impact: Genentech's $750M expansion and continued Intel/ASML presence in Hillsboro's Silicon Forest establishes sustained corporate employment growth and potential talent in-migration to Portland-area tech corridor. Multifamily developers should monitor for corresponding apartment demand and rent growth in Hillsboro/Beaverton submarkets; near-term supply pipeline and absorption will signal whether corporate headcount translates to net population gain or work-from-home attrition. Bridge financing at this pricing suggests hospitality lenders view corridor fundamentals as improving but not yet stabilized.

stories.title: Oxford Properties Buys Six-Property Industrial Portfolio in Phoenix
stories.excerpt: Oxford Properties Group has purchased six industrial properties across three addresses in Phoenix and Tempe, Ariz., near Sky Harbor International Airport. Oxford announced the acquisition of 440 West Fairmont Drive, 800 West Fairmont Drive and 2115 South 11th Avenue, but declined to name the seller or provide the sales price. A source with knowledge of the deal said the 460,000-square-foot light industrial portfolio traded for approximately $100 million. The properties are known as the Sycamore Portfolio and were marketed by a Cushman & Wakefield team of Will Strong, Molly Miller, Jack Stamets, Michael Matchett and Madeline Warren. Revere CRE data, which listed the brokers, and a CBRE brochure indicate that Link Logistics is the seller. “Industrial remains a critical part of Oxford’s U.S. platform and a high-conviction theme for us as we continue to strengthen our vertically integrated operating capabilities in light industrial,” Ankit Bhatt, head of U.S. investments at Oxford Properties, said in a statement. “Our ability to actively recycle capital in this sector allows us to remain responsive to changing market conditions, transact at scale through cycles, and point investment dollars toward highly functional, income-generating assets where we see the strongest relative value.” Oxford’s industrial presence in Phoenix now covers 15 assets and approximately 1.2 million square feet, according to the firm. In 2026, Oxford sold $400 million in properties within its portfolio while investing an equal amount in acquisitions and development, which this transaction is a part of. “Sycamore adds durable income to our portfolio in regional submarkets where we already have a meaningful presence,” Bhatt added. “It also gives our boots-on-the-ground teams an opportunity to leverage their operational expertise to further enhance the performance of these assets over time.” Link Logistics and C&W did not immediately respond to requests for comment. bullets: Oxford Properties acquired six-property 460K SF light industrial portfolio near Phoenix Sky Harbor for ~$100M
Portfolio includes three addresses (Fairmont Drive and S. 11th Ave); marketed by Cushman & Wakefield; Link Logistics seller
Minimal multifamily impact; industrial-focused consolidation near airport logistics hub
stories.summary: Oxford Properties Group purchased a six-property, 460,000-square-foot light industrial portfolio across three addresses in Phoenix and Tempe, Arizona, near Sky Harbor International Airport, for approximately $100 million. Known as the Sycamore Portfolio, the properties were marketed by a Cushman & Wakefield team; Link Logistics was the seller. Oxford highlighted industrial as a critical platform and high-conviction theme.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact to multifamily development. Industrial-focused acquisition near Phoenix Sky Harbor does not signal residential demand or supply changes. However, concentrated industrial investment in Phoenix logistics corridor may indicate strong logistics/last-mile employment growth; if that translates to broader job market expansion in Phoenix metro, indirect demand uplift for worker housing could follow, though timeline and distribution across Phoenix submarkets remain unclear.

stories.title: Truist, Capital One Provide $474M Refi for U.S. Industrial Portfolio
stories.excerpt: Faropoint, a New Jersey-based real estate investment firm specializing in last-mile industrial properties, has secured $474 million to refinance a portfolio of 85 industrial buildings across the U.S. Truist Bank and Capital One provided the debt, which will repay acquisition debt and support future distributions. Moreover, the total deal includes $574 million in total commitments through an $84 million reserve that will distribute capital via an “earn-out” mechanism if the portfolio’s net operating income increases over the term of the loan. “The earn-out is what sets this financing apart,” said Mark DeCesare, head of corporate finance at Faropoint, in a statement. “The structure also gives Fund III meaningful flexibility to execute its business plan, from funding future distributions through the earn-out to adding properties through the accordion.” No broker was listed on the transaction. The refinancing encompasses a total of 85 assets within Faropoint’s Industrial Value Fund III, which has secured $2.2 billion in financing since its June 2024 launch. The assets are located in 12 states, particularly near the markets of Chicago, Philadelphia and New York City. Truist and Faropoint share a fairly close relationship. The firms partnered on a $340 million refinancing in September 2025, and Truist served to co-arrange Faropoint’s $600 million Fund IV acquisition credit facility, which launched in Jan. 2026. “This transaction reflects the strong partnership that Truist and Faropoint have built across multiple funds,” said Alex Rownd, director of real estate corporate banking at Truist. Capital One has also financed two Faropoint funds in recent years. “Faropoint’s experience across its funds has made it a partner we look forward to continuing to grow with,” said Seth Wiener, head of New York regional production at Capital One. Brian Pascus can be reached at bpascus@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Faropoint secured $474M refi plus $84M reserve ($574M total commitments) from Truist and Capital One
Portfolio: 85 last-mile industrial assets across U.S.; earn-out mechanism tied to NOI growth over loan term
Industrial-focused; earn-out structure and $2.2B Fund III commitments signal lender confidence in logistics real estate
stories.summary: Faropoint, a New Jersey-based last-mile industrial specialist, secured $474 million in refinance debt from Truist Bank and Capital One, with total deal commitments of $574 million including an $84 million reserve distributed via earn-out if NOI grows. The financing covers 85 industrial assets within Faropoint's Industrial Value Fund III, which has secured $2.2 billion in commitments since June 2024 launch. Earn-out structure provides flexibility for distributions and acquisitions.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact to multifamily development. Last-mile industrial financing trends do not inform apartment demand or supply. However, robust capital availability for industrial portfolios ($2.2B for Fund III) and earn-out structures signal that lenders remain active in real estate despite higher rate environment, suggesting broader credit availability may support multifamily refinancing if asset performance holds.

stories.title: California Rejects Construction Fast-Track Measure, Approves Billions for Housing
stories.excerpt: California voters rejected Proposition 45, a ballot measure that would have streamlined environmental reviews for housing, infrastructure and other development projects, the Associated Press projected. Backed by the California Chamber of Commerce and major developers, the measure sought to accelerate construction by imposing tighter deadlines on environmental reviews and legal challenges under the California Environmental Quality Act. Opponents argued the changes would weaken environmental protections, limit public participation and encourage suburban sprawl. Some groups saw it as a Trojan horse designed to open the door for more data centers. Californians also voted 60.9 percent to 39.1 percent for Proposition 1, authorizing $11.25 billion in general obligation bonds to finance affordable housing construction, rehabilitation and homeownership assistance. Of that amount, $10 billion will support housing programs, including multifamily rental developments, while $1.25 billion will finance home loans for veterans. The measure also provides funding for supportive housing, student housing and low-income homebuyers. State analysts estimate the bonds could support approximately 40,000 rental units and help 40,000 households purchase homes. California voters, too, approved Proposition 37, authorizing up to $25 billion in revenue bonds to provide down-payment assistance to middle-income homebuyers purchasing newly constructed homes. Eligible households can earn up to twice their area’s median income, adjusted for household size. Unlike Proposition 1, the program would be financed through bonds backed by borrower repayments rather than the state’s general fund. Also, Los Angeles voters approved Measure TE, creating a one-time exemption from the city’s Measure ULA transfer tax, commonly known as the “mansion tax,” for properties damaged or destroyed in the January 2025 Palisades fire. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: California voters rejected Prop 45 (environmental streamlining) but approved Prop 1: $11.25B housing bonds
$10B supports multifamily rental, $1.25B for veteran home loans; 60.9% to 39.1% approval margin
CEQA timeline remains unchanged; housing subsidy capital available but permitting timeline risk persists in California
stories.summary: California voters rejected Proposition 45, which would have accelerated environmental reviews and legal challenges under CEQA for housing and infrastructure projects, while approving Proposition 1 by a 60.9% to 39.1% margin. Proposition 1 authorizes $11.25 billion in general obligation bonds for housing programs, with $10 billion supporting multifamily rental developments and related supportive housing, and $1.25 billion for veteran home loans. The rejection of Prop 45 leaves CEQA timelines and processes intact.
stories.impact: Prop 1's $10B multifamily subsidy capital pool will support affordable and mixed-income development, especially in high-cost metros (LA, SF Bay, San Diego), increasing competition for scarce entitled sites and potentially compressing market-rate development returns. Rejection of Prop 45 preserves CEQA litigation risk and long approval timelines, increasing cost of capital for projects with extended entitlement uncertainty. Combined effect: California multifamily developers face cheaper debt and grant capital for affordable/mixed-income but higher entitlement friction and legal risk; focus will shift to shovel-ready sites and partnerships with nonprofits accessing bond proceeds.
